"use client";

import { useState } from 'react';

import { Button, Group, Menu, Menubar, Stack } from '@mantine/core';

function Demo() {
  const [openIndex, setOpenIndex] = useState<number | null>(null);

  return (
    <Stack>
      <Group>
        <Button variant="default" onClick={() => setOpenIndex(0)}>
          Open File
        </Button>
        <Button variant="default" onClick={() => setOpenIndex(1)}>
          Open Edit
        </Button>
        <Button variant="default" onClick={() => setOpenIndex(null)}>
          Close all
        </Button>
      </Group>

      <Menubar openIndex={openIndex} onOpenChange={setOpenIndex}>
        <Menubar.Menu width={220}>
          <Menubar.Target>File</Menubar.Target>
          <Menubar.Dropdown>
            <Menu.Item>New file</Menu.Item>
            <Menu.Item>Save</Menu.Item>
          </Menubar.Dropdown>
        </Menubar.Menu>

        <Menubar.Menu width={220}>
          <Menubar.Target>Edit</Menubar.Target>
          <Menubar.Dropdown>
            <Menu.Item>Undo</Menu.Item>
            <Menu.Item>Redo</Menu.Item>
          </Menubar.Dropdown>
        </Menubar.Menu>
      </Menubar>
    </Stack>
  );
}
const RendynExampleComponent = Demo;
export function RendynExample() { return <RendynExampleComponent  />; }

# Mantine menubar

5 published Mantine menubar examples with complete pinned source and MIT attribution.

## Installation

- Complete MIT usage examples extracted from the upstream demo code template; documentation configurator machinery is excluded.
- Mount MantineProvider once at your client application root and import @mantine/core/styles.css. The returned preview wrapper is a standalone example; reuse an existing provider when integrating.

- Copy every returned file and preserve the MIT licence notice.
- Render the returned preview.tsx example, or integrate the example into your existing provider.
